source.title: From Zero to Hero: An Open LLM Ecosystem for Armenian
source.authors: Erik Arakelyan; Khatun Avetisyan; M. Davtyan; Heghine Grigoryan; N. Khachatryan; Hayk Shahsuvaryan; Henrik Sergoyan; Vahan Martirosyan

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures loss across model sizes and fits a power law, but uses bits-per-byte on Armenian panels rather than the original studies’ held-out cross-entropy measure. It also tests an independently trained larger model against the fit.
record.gate_note: The scaling ladder and its held-out confirmation bear on V1 and V2. The paper uses Chinchilla-budget runs but does not compare parameter/token allocations at fixed compute. Other scaling-related statements in the text are background or citations and are not recorded as results here.
record.test_reason: The study trains a four-rung compute-optimal ladder (70M–1B) on an Armenian union recipe and fits a three-parameter power law to held-out mean panel bits-per-byte. It then checks the fit's prediction on an independently trained 1.3B model. Bits-per-byte is a rescaled held-out cross-entropy and the procedure matches the originals, so this is mainly a new setting (low-resource Armenian, SentencePiece tokenizer, Megatron) rather than a new method. T2 is also defensible.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors use the ladder to argue that their 160M/410M data-ablation conclusions are properties of the data, not of the 410M scale. They also argue the smooth power-law fit shows no residual duplication or contamination being exploited. The 0.47% prediction error on the held-out 1.3B model is their headline evidence.
record.recipe_differences: Measures bits-per-byte on Armenian evaluation panels rather than held-out cross-entropy; fits a three-parameter curve along a union-recipe, compute-optimal scaling ladder and checks a held-out model.
record.method_sensitivity: The results are for one union recipe and a single displayed power-law fit; alternative data recipes and fitting choices are not compared.

fits_no_version.finding: Data-recipe rankings from 410M ablations transfer exactly to 1.3B runs, with the union's lead widening from 0.013 to 0.035 bpb (Table 11).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative data-recipe rankings measured at small scale are preserved at larger scale.

record.problems: The ladder has four fitted rungs over 70M–1B parameters and uses one Armenian union recipe. Compute, token budget, and parameter count are not independently varied. The held-out confirmation is only 30% larger than the largest fitted model; seed spreads are reported only as at or below 0.003 bpb.

untested.parts: Several orders of magnitude: N spans about 1.2 orders (70M–1B). Parameters, tokens and compute are never varied separately, since N and D grow together along the compute-optimal ladder.
Extrapolation by orders of magnitude: the held-out model is only 30% larger than the largest fitted rung.
No fixed-compute comparison of parameter/token splits.
Repetition is measured (Table 4), but no power-law fit to epochs is made. No other modality is tested.
No downstream-vs-scale relation; downstream evaluation is only for CPT models.
No comparison of fitting choices or setups.

missing.what: Mean bpb versus epochs of ArmWeb repetition (1/2/4/8 epochs) at 160M (0.710→0.572) and 410M (0.649→0.526). Gains shrink per doubling and are called consistent with data-constrained scaling laws, but no power-law fit is reported, so the power-law form for repeated data cannot be determined.
missing.locator: Section 2.1, Effect of data repetition; Table 4

record.verdict_notes: The record's two limits_scope labels described untested parts (narrow range, small extrapolation, no independent variation of N/D), so they were moved to untested per the rules. The authors' reading of a smooth fit as evidence against contamination is an inference, not a test. Seed spreads are at or below 0.003 bpb. The study is a resource paper; scaling is a side validation.

versions.untested_parts: The ladder varies parameters along compute-optimal budgets, so it does not isolate parameter count while holding tokens and compute independently controlled, nor test the claim over several orders of magnitude.
The confirmation model is 30% larger than the largest fitted model, not orders of magnitude larger.
No comparison of alternative parameter/token allocations at a fixed compute budget, or fitted allocation trend, is reported.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No other modality or training regime is tested for the power-law form.
No downstream performance scaling relationship is tested.
The study reports one fit and one recipe; it does not compare fitting choices or test whether curves bend away from a power law under other setups.

rows.subject: union-recipe model (1B rung)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the union recipe as part of the scaling ladder; mean panel bits-per-byte measured.
rows.uncertainty: Seed spreads at or below 0.003 bpb
rows.note: The ladder points use Chinchilla-budget runs.

rows.subject: union-recipe scaling ladder (four-rung fit)
rows.operation_detail: Fit a three-parameter power law to mean panel bits-per-byte versus parameter count across the four ladder rungs.
rows.value: bpb(N) = 4.9×10^5 N^-0.795 + 0.439; fits all four rungs within 0.0015 bpb at full precision
rows.note: The displayed coefficients are rounded; the full-precision fit is stated to be released with the code.
rows.check: A three-parameter fit to four points leaves one degree of freedom, so the 0.0015 bpb fit error is weak evidence of power-law form on its own. The mean panel also includes FW2-test and hyWiki panels, on which the CulturaX half of the union recipe is contaminated.

rows.subject: independently trained union-recipe 1.3B confirmation model
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean panel bits-per-byte on an independently trained confirmation model and compared it with the fit from smaller ladder runs.
rows.measure: Mean panel bits-per-byte; fitted prediction error
rows.note: The authors describe this as a fifth, independently trained, larger model.
rows.check: SP_tokens is listed as not stated. Appendix C/Table 11 reports 1.3B union runs at 27.6B SP tokens with mean 0.470, matching the measured 0.4697, so this is likely the same run. Record 27.6B SP tokens with that caveat.
